key_insight: A tabulated-chemistry RANS model that explicitly includes preferential and differential diffusion can capture the key thermo-diffusive behavior of lean hydrogen flames much more faithfully than unity-Lewis or table-only approximations.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable and cost-effective CFD prediction of lean hydrogen combustors where flame length, heat release, and stability are strongly affected by diffusion-driven instabilities.
method: Extended a tabulated-chemistry model to RANS with mixture-averaged diffusion and Soret effect.
Solved transport equations for progress variable and mixture fraction with a presumed-PDF turbulence–chemistry closure.
Compared preferential/differential diffusion, unity-Lewis, and thermo-diffusion-only variants against DNS at Re = 5500 and 11000.
evidence_signal: Against DNS for a lean premixed H2-air slot burner, the model reproduces flame length, heat-release distribution, and the characteristic equivalence-ratio and super-adiabatic temperature branches at both Reynolds numbers.
watch_item: Performance still depends on turbulence closures for turbulent diffusion, scalar dissipation rate, and Reynolds stresses, so calibration and model choice remain important.
paper_title: Preferential and differential diffusion in RANS simulation of lean hydrogen flames with tabulated chemistry
